positioning:
He builds and ships real web software for paying clients, which is more than most junior applicants can say, and the modern React and Next.js stack he works in is exactly what postings ask for. The honest shape of the gap is that agency work is broad and shallow where product work is narrow and deep: he has built many things once rather than one thing for two years, and he has not worked inside a team codebase with code review, tests and a release process.

Say that plainly rather than letting an interviewer discover it. Most postings in this lane grade Tier A or Tier B, and the two recurring gaps are automated testing and relational SQL, both shared with other lanes, which makes them the highest-leverage things to close anywhere in this search.
interview_watch: Expect a code exercise and expect a conversation about a project you chose. Pick K2_Press or the automation pipeline rather than a tutorial project, and be ready to say what you would do differently now. Expect a question about working with other people's code, which is the real gap, so answer it honestly with how you handle unfamiliar repos rather than claiming team experience you do not have.
pr_note: 21232 is on the North Bay RCIP list and was on MPNP as of v3.1 (re-verify). 21231 is on the Steinbach RCIP list. AIP covers the lane, and Ontario's Workforce Priority stream takes any of these with a qualifying offer. Strong codes, all TEER 1.
not_required: Anything requiring a computer science degree as a hard prerequisite, which is a credential-gate drop rather than a skill gap.
